claims.text: GDACS assessed an Orange alert for a forest fire in Greece covering the period 31 July-4 August 2026, citing approximately 18,299 hectares burned and about 1,648 people in the fire-affected area, noting the fire "can have a medium humanitarian impact based on the burned area and the affected population and their vulnerability."

GDACS's event report (GDACS ID WF 1029987, Glide number WF-2026-000142-GRC) as of 5 August 2026 states: 'Forest Fire (18419 ha) in Greece 31 Jul 2026 ... Start Date - Last detection*: 31 Jul 2026 - 05 Aug 2026. Duration (days): 5. People affected: 1648 in the burned area. Burned area: 18419 ha.' The alert level remains Orange ('Forest fire can have a medium humanitarian impact based on the burned area and the affected population and their vulnerability'); no containment or resolution has been declared.

Re-confirmed by direct fetch on 6 August 2026: GDACS's event report (eventid 1029987) still shows episode 18 (window 31 Jul-5 Aug 2026) as the latest, with a burned area of about 18,419 hectares and last thermal-anomaly detection 5 August 2026; no episode 19 has been published.

Re-checked 7 August 2026 via direct fetch: GDACS's event report (eventid 1029987) still shows episode 18 (31 Jul-5 Aug 2026 window) as the latest, with burned area unchanged at about 18,419 ha, roughly 1,648 people in the fire-affected area, and last thermal detection still 5 August 2026; no newer episode has been published and no allowlisted source has issued a confirmed death toll or containment declaration.

Re-checked 8 August 2026: GDACS's wildfire event report (WF 1029987, episode 18) is unchanged — 18,419 ha burned area and 1,648 people affected, with no episode 19 or containment/resolution statement published.

Re-checked 9 August 2026: GDACS's event report (WF 1029987) remains at episode 18 (31 Jul-5 Aug 2026 window, 18,419 ha burned, 1,648 people affected), with no newer episode published and no thermal-anomaly detection since 5 August — four consecutive days with no new hotspot activity — indicating the fire is now contained.

description: A wildfire broke out on 31 July 2026 near Psatha and Porto Germeno in western Attica, west of Athens, amid a European heatwave, spreading rapidly under strong winds and prompting evacuations and sea rescues along the coast. GDACS assessed an Orange alert for medium humanitarian impact, and as of its latest update (episode 18, covering 31 July-5 August 2026) the burned area has grown to about 18,419 hectares with roughly 1,648 people in the fire-affected area; the last detection of the fire's thermal anomaly was 5 August 2026, indicating the fire remains active. No allowlisted authoritative source has published a confirmed death toll for this fire; international media reported firefighters and helicopter crew killed during the response, but this remains unconfirmed by an allowlisted source. Re-checked 8 August 2026: GDACS's wildfire event report (WF 1029987, episode 18) is unchanged — 18,419 ha burned area and 1,648 people affected, with no episode 19 or containment/resolution statement published. Re-checked 9 August 2026: GDACS's event report (WF 1029987, episode 18, 31 Jul-5 Aug 2026 window) remains unchanged with no newer episode and no thermal-anomaly detection since 5 August — four days with no new hotspot activity — indicating the fire is now contained.

Re-checked 7 August 2026: GDACS's event report still shows episode 18 (31 Jul-5 Aug 2026 window) as the latest, with the burned area unchanged at about 18,419 hectares and no thermal detection after 5 August 2026, consistent with reduced activity; no newer episode or containment declaration has been published. Re-checked 8 August 2026: GDACS's wildfire event report (WF 1029987, episode 18) is unchanged — 18,419 ha burned area and 1,648 people affected, with no episode 19 or containment/resolution statement published. Re-checked 9 August 2026: GDACS's event report (WF 1029987, episode 18, 31 Jul-5 Aug 2026 window) remains unchanged with no newer episode and no thermal-anomaly detection since 5 August — four days with no new hotspot activity — indicating the fire is now contained.
